source: Reviewed per USAG number against the Xcel CoP 2022-2028 (General D-F; Bars/Beam/Floor Chapter 2 'Elements considered different / the same'; element-table box notes) and, for E elements and as a tiebreaker, the USAG Development Program 2026-2030 box notes. 'same': listed versions that count as one element; versions not in a group are different elements. Reasons are our own words. 'unsure': calls for the WAG rules lead to confirm.

unsure.question: Healy 1 1/2 to L grip is done on one arm; grouped as same per the Code's grip example (cast handstand 1 1/2 vs same to L grip). Does the one-arm (Healy) technique make it different from the 1 1/2 pirouette? v1 also covers a 1/1, which would differ by turn.

Twisting flic-flac mount to clear support vs through LB handstand: best guess different (handstand rule); or is the second just an allowed option of the same element?

Hop-initiated 1/1 vs one-arm 1/1 with arm flair, both from an L-grip front giant: same turn, but one-arm support and separate names. Same or different? (Elsewhere the Code bundles in-handstand and one-arm Healy turns of equal degree.)

unsure.question: Is a leap mount that ends lowered into a scale the same element as the plain leap/jump mount? (v1 also covers a two-foot jump, which would differ by take-off.)
Leg-swing mounts with 180 deg total turn ending in front support vs straddle sit: same element?
Leap mount to cross split sit vs switch-leg leap mount to straddle sit: same element, or does the leg change / end sit make them different?
Chest/head stand mount vs shoulder stand mount: same element?
One-arm handstand mount vs handstand shifted to one arm and lowered to straddle support: does the different entry/exit make them different?
The strict same-number default groups the ring-leap catch (v5) with the 1/4-turn split leap (v1), and the Heinrich (v3) with the Sweetin (v4). Are these really the same element?
Switch leap with 1/4 turn landing in front support: same as the plain switch leap?
Switch side leap vs switch leap taken from a side stand: same element?
v1 allows 1/2 or 3/4 turn; v2 is 3/4. Is a 3/4 pike jump from side the same as one from cross, and does 1/2 vs 3/4 differ?
Switch leap with 1/2+ turn vs switch side leap with an extra 1/2-3/4 turn: turn totals overlap. Same or different?
1/2 turn on one foot vs heel-snap 1/2 turn (on two feet): same element for VP?
1 1/2 vs 1 3/4 tuck turn finishing in a kneel: is the extra 1/4 a different degree of turn, or an added 1/4 that does not count?
Back walkover to one-arm handstand vs one-arm handstand hold: does the entrance make them different? (The rule only says same entrance and exit = same.)
Forward roll vs whip forward roll vs shoulder roll with hands: same element?
Dive roll vs hand-supported shoulder roll through vertical: same or different?
Front walkover from straddle support (swing to handstand) vs from a stand; and alternating hand support vs both hands: same element?
Tuck-open vs pike-open flic to straddle sit (v2 also allows a gainer, one-leg take-off): same element?

The strict default makes all aerial cartwheel variants (side landing, Perry 1/4 turn-out, Clore from kneel, Marinez leg hold) one element. Correct, or are any (especially Clore and Marinez) different?
Front handspring vs front headspring dismount: same element?
Front aerial dismount vs aerial round-off dismount: same element?
Front tuck mount vs handspring then front tuck mount from the end: does the added handspring make them different?
v2 is a stretched sideward roll with a full 360 deg body rotation; does that count as a 1/1 turn (different from v1, which has none or 1/2), or is it the same sideward roll?
Backward roll vs backward shoulder roll: same element? (Same question as 6.101 v3.)
Switch ring leap vs switch double-stag ring leap taken from a side stand: same element? (Same question as 2.405.)

boxes.reason: No turn vs full turn: different degree of turn.
Both are switch leaps (one-foot take-off) with no turn; only the leg shape differs (wolf vs stag), which is not a listed criterion and matches the stag/split-variation-is-same note.
Rond-de-jambe switch is normally done without turn, so it differs from the half-turn switch by degree of turn. If it is done with the half turn it would arguably be the same element (see unsure).
Quarter-turn switch-side vs switch-side with an added turn to stand vs half turn in the horizontal plane to prone: treated as different degrees/kinds of turn, each printed as its own entry.
No turn vs half turn: different degree of turn.
Two-foot jump with full turn vs one-foot leap with 1.5 turns: different take-off and different turn.
Hitch-kick vs cabriole. The Xcel box is silent, but the 2026 Development code box says all four (fwd/back of each) are different; followed that.
Both one-foot take-off with half turn total (two quarter turns vs one half); no printed criterion separates them, so same by default.
One-foot tour jete to ring (half turn) vs two-foot stag-ring jump with full turn: different take-off and turn.
Both full turn, but one-foot leap vs two-foot jump: leaps and jumps under one number are different.
Two-foot jump vs one-foot leap: leaps and jumps under one number are different.
One-foot leap with no turn vs two-foot jump with full turn: different take-off and turn.
Half twist vs full twist into the dive roll: different degree of turn.
Box note: every backward-roll variation counts as a different element.
One-foot take-off handspring vs two-foot take-off flyspring; take-off criterion applied by analogy (see unsure).
Arabian handspring has a half twist, flyspring has none: different degree of turn.
Box note: cartwheel, aerial cartwheel and butterfly variations all count as different elements.
Tucked vs piked/stretched salto: different body position.
Double back tucked vs piked: different body position.
Double arabian without vs with half twist: different degree of turn (Development Program E box).
Full twist vs 1.5 twist: different degree of turn (Development Program E box).
No twist vs full twist vs double twist: different degree of turn (Development Program E box).

unsure.question: Switch leap to wolf vs switch stag leap: no printed note. Treated as same (shape only). Should different leg shapes in one box count separately?
Straight-leg hitch-kick with two quarter turns vs tour jete: both one-foot take-off, half turn total, no box note. Same by default rule, or different skills?
Xcel box has no note; the 2026 Development code says hitch-kick and cabriole (fwd/back) are all different. Does that note apply to Xcel?
Variant 2 (rond-de-jambe switch) covers both no-turn and half-turn forms. Without turn it differs from variant 1; with half turn it may be the same. How should the single id be treated?

Quarter-turn switch-side vs the half/three-quarter turn-to-stand version differ by only a quarter turn in the half-turn case; and the turn-to-stand vs horizontal-plane-to-prone versions both have a half turn. Are any of these the same?

Front handspring (one-foot take-off) vs flyspring (two-foot take-off), both may land on one foot. Take-off criterion is written only for leaps/jumps/hops. Same or different? (Low stakes: both are hand-support flight elements.)
Head/neck kips have hand support and usually a brief flight, but also support on head/neck (cf. dive roll not counting as flight). Excluded from handSupportFlight; should they be included?
Cartwheel record includes a with-flight option and the no-hands aerial cartwheel. Excluded from handSupportFlight because the usual cartwheel has no flight; should a flighted cartwheel qualify?
Record merges round-off (hand support) with free aerial round-off (no hands). Included in handSupportFlight as a round-off; the aerial form alone would not qualify.
Record includes a jump onto the hands (brief flight before hand support) but mostly kick/press handstands with no flight. Excluded from handSupportFlight; should the jump form qualify?
